title: Give the report cache's callers the source's own exception

blocks.text: The reporting service reads report texts from a file share that is slow, so it keeps each text in memory after the first read. The cache is meant to be built on `Map.computeIfAbsent`. Its callers already handle failures by type: a `FileNotFoundException` becomes "no such report" for the user, any other `IOException` becomes "try again later", and an unchecked exception is a bug that goes to the error tracker.

Write `get(...)` and `fetchForCache(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/ReportCache.java`. When you're done, `get` caches each text, and when the source fails, the caller receives exactly the exception the source threw, checked or unchecked. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: each report is fetched from the source once, then served from the cache
a fetch that fails makes the call fail with an IOException, and other reports still load
the caller receives the very IOException the source threw, so it can catch the specific subtype
an unchecked exception from the source reaches the caller as it was thrown

origin.section: A Checked Exception Can't Leave a `Function`: Wrap It in the Lambda, Unwrap It at Your Boundary

concepts: A lambda for a standard functional interface can't throw a checked exception, so it wraps it, and the enclosing method unwraps it before returning so callers catch the original checked type.
